calls.head: The Senators’ power play has a target
calls.body: The Senators’ power play is near the top of the league, and the Bruins’ kill is near the bottom of the league. Every trip to the box hurts the Bruins more than most.
calls.call: The Senators’ power play creates at least their usual 7.8 expected goals per 60.
calls.nums: Ottawa 9th for power play (7.8 expected goals per 60) · Boston 27th for penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Ottawa had only 0:15 of power-play time, too little to judge.

calls.head: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams
calls.body: The Senators and the Bruins are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 110.
calls.nums: Hit score (100 is league average): Ottawa 114 (3rd), Boston 106 (10th)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game was rarely close, and hit rates are only counted in close games, so this one can’t be judged.

calls.head: The Senators hunt better looks than the Bruins
calls.body: On shot quality, Ottawa is the league’s best and Boston is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Senators’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Bruins’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 1 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot was, Ottawa had 5.3% a shot and Boston 7.8% a shot. Coming in, Ottawa was at 7.0% a shot and Boston at 5.9% a shot.
calls.usual: OTT 7.0% a shot · BOS 5.9% a shot
calls.tonight: OTT 5.3% a shot · BOS 7.8% a shot

BOS.head: We gave Boston only a 34% chance, and it went the way we feared.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 66% chance, and Ottawa delivered.

surprises.head: Ottawa shut down Boston’s power play
surprises.body: Boston’s power play created 2.8 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.8 and a league average of 7.5. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

surprises.head: Ottawa couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Ottawa’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 5.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 7.0% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 10 games.
surprises.flipped: The Senators hunt better looks than the Bruins

story.head: The Senators beat the Bruins
paras: Tim Stützle scored twice, opening the scoring midway through the first.
The chances were closer than the score.
